idiom_name: view registry keyed by view handle + factory by view type + notify-all change propagation
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep one registry that maps a view handle (id, name or object reference) to a live view, and make the handler the only component that adds to it, removes from it and iterates it - creation goes through a factory keyed by view type and disposal is the matching removal, so the registry never accumulates stale entries. Clients receive handles instead of views and issue view commands (open, switch, close, layout meta-commands) against the handler, while the factory keeps the handler closed for modification as view types are added. Change propagation is inverted: the model asks the handler to refresh and the handler decides which views are affected - tracking dependencies or at least coalescing redraws instead of walking every view on every mutation. Keep per-view state in the views, per-document state in the model, and only topology and policy in the handler; mutate the registry through a single UI thread or a command queue as soon as views can be opened or closed from other threads.
code_sketch:
handler = ViewHandler(factories_by_view_type)
id = handler.open("chart", model)        # factory creates, registers, activates
handler.switch_to(id)
handler.tile()                            # meta-command over the whole set
model.on_change = handler.notify_views     # model no longer publishes to views

handler.close(id)                         # remove from the registry first,
                                          # then dispose - never the other way round
pitfalls: A registry that is added to on open but not cleaned on close keeps disposed views alive and keeps notifying them.
Handing views to clients instead of handles lets a caller keep or dispose a view behind the handler's back.
Iterating the registry while a notification causes a view to open or close another view corrupts the iteration.
Notifying every view on every model change, without dependency tracking or coalescing, turns each data change into a full redraw of the UI.

Wrong move: keeping a second list of open views in the controller or shell beside the handler's registry -> the two collections drift apart as views close, and layout or close-all commands act on ghosts -> instead let one registry be the single source of truth, or delegate it wholesale to the platform's handler (MDICLIENT, QMdiArea, JDesktopPane/DesktopManager) so no private form collection is needed.

Wrong move: disposing the view object before removing it from the registry -> teardown callbacks and in-flight notifications reach a half-dead view, or the close path aborts and leaks the entry -> instead make close strictly remove-then-dispose so registration and disposal stay a matched pair.

Wrong move: broadcasting every model mutation to every open view for simplicity -> each keystroke repaints the table, chart and outline in lockstep, and a view that mutates the model on update spirals into re-entrant notify storms -> instead record which part of the model each view observes, let the handler route only the affected views, and coalesce refreshes per frame or tick.
